One of the main challenges to be overcome is to control the qualityof the large parts printed as their inspection is complicated due to their large dimensions.Thisactivity aims at development of in-situ monitoring to allow to control the manufacturing process(e.g. cooling rates and associatedmicrostructure, geometrical deviation, lack of fusion, residualstresses, atmosphere and oxide creation) directly during manufacturing.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Establishment of overview of the most advanced Direct Energy Deposition (DED) processesfor large part production for launcher applications- Identification of target process and two materials of interest for launcher applications- Definition of specific parameters to be monitored including materials specific issues such ascooling rates for Inconel, and oxygen pick up for Titanium- Special consideration to monitor surface and sub-surface defects as some of the large partscannot be post processed or machined after DED processes.- Development of specific NDI methods for all identified parameters- Verification of NDI methods capabilities at samples level in comparison with destructive analysis- Production of several parts with varying geometry to assess residual stresses and geometrical deviations- Manufacturing of large part to demonstrate the capabilities of the NDI at component level. A defect catalogue for the DED process selected and the materials tested is aimed to be be created- Definition of a roadmap for the implementation of in process corrections when defects are detectedActivity serves the area of low cost and low mass solutions for launchers.
